Total number of questions — 20
Illegal encroachment of wakf
properties
*81. SHRIMATI NAZNIN
FARUQUE: Will the Minister of
MINORITY AFFAIRS be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that a number of
wakf properties are illegally encroached;
(b) if so, the details thereof;
(c) the number of applications received
for removal of illegal encroachments;
(d) the details thereof; and
(e) the steps being taken by Government
in this regard?
Financial assistance and scholarships
to minorities
*82. SHRI TARUN VIJAY: Will the
Minister of MINORITY AFFAIRS be
pleased to state:
(a) whether there is any plan to provide
financial assistance and scholarships to
women and students belonging to those
communities which are in numerical
minority in the States like Jammu and
Kashmir and in the North East;
(b) if so, the details thereof; and
(c) if not, the reasons therefor and
whether any scheme is available to such
minorities?
Schemes for repair and renovation of
ponds
*83. SHRI AAYANUR MANJU-
NA THA: Will the Minister of WATER
RESOURCES be pleased to state:
(a) the details of the Central schemes
for repair and renovation of ponds, State-
wise, particularly in Karnataka; and
(b) the steps being taken by
Government to expedite the
implementation of the programmes/
schemes and the funds earmarked for the
same during the last three years?
Wastage of FCI stocks
*84. SHRI P. RAJEEVE: Will the
Minister of CONSUMER AFFAIRS,
FOOD AND PUBLIC DISTRIBUTION
be pleased to state:
(a) whether any of the stocks in the
godowns of the Food Corporation of India
(FCI) have been ruined or destroyed during
the last three years; and

(b) if so, the details thereof?
Contaminated drinking water in
Madhya Pradesh
†*85. DR. VIJAYLAXMI SADHO:
Will the Minister of DRINKING WATER
AND SANITA TION be pleased to state:
(a) whether the condition of ground
water level and the quality of water in
Madhya Pradesh is alarming;
(b) whether the people living in many
Scheduled Areas of the State are drinking
water contaminated with arsenic, fluoride
and other harmful chemicals;
(c) if so, the remedial measures taken
by Government in this regard; and
(d) the details of action being taken by
Government to provide pure drinking
water?
Production and import of coal
*86. SHRI DHIRAJ PRASAD SAHU:
Will the Minister of COAL be pleased to
state:
(a) the production, in tonnes, by each
subsidiary of Coal India Ltd. and other coal
companies during each of the last three
years;
(b) the quantum and value of coal
imported during the said period;
(c) whether Government has taken any
effective steps to improve the quality of
coal and check its imports into the country;
and
(d) if so, the details thereof?
Recommendations of Task Force on
coal allocation
*87. SHRI MANSUKH L.
MANDA VIYA: Will the Minister of
COAL be pleased to state:
(a) what action has been taken, as on
date, by the Central Government on the
recommendations of Task Force
constituted to allocate coal to Gujarat
Government from nearby collieries, to
minimize unwanted transport cost;
(b) the details of the recommendations
of this Task Force; and
(c) how much quantity of coal would
be allocated to the State Government from
various collieries for the next five years,
colliery-wise?
Mandatory set top boxes for viewing
TV channels
*88. SHRI SANJAY RAUT: Will the
Minister of INFORMATION AND
BROADCASTING be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government has made set
top boxes mandatory for viewing TV
channels across the country;
(b) if so, how many metro cities have
been covered in the first phase and how
many would be covered in the second phase;
(c) how much revenue Government has
earned on each set top box; and
(d) whether Government is mulling to
provide subsidy to the families who can't
afford to install set top boxes and pay
monthly subscription?
Prices of vegetables
*89. SHRIMATI KUSUM RAI: Will
the Minister of CONSUMER AFFAIRS,
FOOD AND PUBLIC DISTRIBUTION
be pleased to state:
(a) the details of rise in prices of
vegetables during the last three months;
(b) whether Government is aware that

27
price of onion in wholesale market has just
doubled in a fortnight;
(c) if so, the details thereof, State-wise;
(d) the reasons for sudden rise in price
of onion;
(e) whether Government has taken
steps to bring down the price of onion in
wholesale market;
(f) if so, the details thereof; and
(g) if not, the reasons therefor?
Aadhaar-enabled payments under
MGNREGA

Impact of coal mining
621. DR. NAJMA A. HEPTULLA:
Will the Minister of COAL be pleased to
state:
(a) whether Government has taken note
of adverse impact of coal mining on social
forestry, environment and health of people
living in and around the coal mining areas/
belts;
(b) if so, the details thereof along with
the corrective steps taken by Government
in this regard;
(c) whether it is a fact that locals/tribals
are being forced to evict their areas for coal
mining operations; and
(d) if so, the details thereof including
Madhya Pradesh, location-wise and coal
mine-wise?
Allocation for CIL and its subsidiaries
622. SHRI P. BHA TTACHARYA: Will
the Minister of COAL be pleased to state:
(a) the plans and measures of
Government to make the Coal India Limited
(CIL) and all its subsidiaries to be profitable
and to achieve its annual target production
and distribution;
(b) this total amount allocated for CIL
and its subsidiaries during the last three
years for welfare schemes of the employees
and mine workers; and
(c) the steps taken by Government to
provide safety and security of mine workers
working in hostile conditions prevailing in
some of the coal mines?
De-allocation of coal blocks
623. SHRI PRAKASH
JAV ADEKAR:
SHRI C.M. RAMESH:
Will the Minister of COAL be pleased
to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that the Supreme
Court has questioned the authority of the
Centre in allocating/de-allocating of coal
blocks;
(b) whether it is also a fact that the
Centre lacks legal sanction to decide who
should be allocated the coal blocks in the

143
States, particularly as per the Mines and
Minerals Development and Regulation Act;
and
(c) if so, the basis on which the Centre
is allocating the coal blocks?
Coal excavation by SCCL
624. SHRI DEVENDER GOUD T.:
Will the Minister of COAL be pleased to
state:
(a) the quality and grades of coal being
excavated by Singareni Collieries Company
Ltd. (SCCL) in Andhra Pradesh;
(b) the details of companies to which
SCCL was supplying coal during the last
five years, year-wise, company-wise and
quantity-wise;
(c) whether it is a fact that NTPC has
now decided to pay coal, according to its
quality;
(d) whether it is also a fact that SCCL
would lose ` 300 crores due to above
decision; and
(e) if so, how SCCL is planning to go
ahead in this regard?
Coal scam
625. SHRI RAJKUMAR DHOOT:
Will the Minister of COAL be pleased to
state:
(a) the number of coal blocks scrapped,
so far, by Government after coalgate scam
was unearthed, with details thereof;
(b) whether it is a fact that Government
has decided to re-allocate those coal blocks
to public sector NTPC;
(c) if so, the details thereof;
(d) whether Government proposes to
take similar decision with regard to other
scrapped coal blocks; and
(e) if not, the reasons therefor?
Coal supply for power plant at
Goindwal Sahib
626. DR. KANWAR DEEP SINGH:
Will the Minister of COAL be pleased to
state:
(a) whether coal supply for upcoming
power plant at Goindwal Sahib in Punjab,
which is likely to be operational by March,
2013, would be met from the Tokisud coal
block in Jharkhand;
(b) if so, the details thereof;
(c) the current status of coal mining in
the block;
(d) whether there are complications
regarding the same as some areas of this
block falls under forest cover;
(e) whether this can delay the
operations of this power plant; and
(f) if so, the details thereof and the
proposed plan of action?
Status of CIL’s FSA with power
companies
627. SHRI RAJKUMAR DHOOT:
Will the Minister of COAL be pleased to
state the present status of Fuel Supply
Agreements (FSA) signed with the Coal
India Ltd. by power companies?
Acquiring coal blocks by private firms
628. SHRI SANJAY RAUT: Will the
Minister of COAL be pleased to state:
(a) the number of private firms which
misrepresented their net worth to secure
coal blocks; and
(b) the action taken by CBI against them
and officials of the Ministries of Coal,
Power and Steel who have colluded with
private firms to allocate coal blocks?

144

blocks

Minister of COAL be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that irregularities
are found in the allocation of coal blocks in
the country;
(b) if so, the details thereof;
(c) whether the Supreme Court had
taken cognizance of such irregularities;
(d) if so, the observations of the

Government thereto;
